texto: 3What's installedhyprlandper-monitoreDP + DPThe launcherThe compositor settingsThe power menuTwo panels, and the login screen only on one of them.The machine has two: the built-in panel and an external one over DP. Each carries its own name, resolution and scale in the compositor's configuration, and the built-in one is the primary.That is why the login screen only ever appears on the internal panel: the external one is not a login target. texto: 5The dockrust-dockrustgtk430 fpsThe dockThe strip along the bottom edge. Ours, in Rust and GTK4, compiled during the install.A dock in Rust with a GTK4 interface, compiled from source by the installer. There is no package to install and nothing to update afterwards. --skip-rust-dock skips the build if you would rather put something else there.It has two halves. The left one holds the applications you have anchored; the right one fills with whatever else is open. Windows appear and disappear in real time at 30 fps, because the dock asks the compositor instead of guessing.Drag an icon to reorder it. Hover a window for a preview rendered with grim. Clicking focuses, clicking again minimizes.It takes its own options from the command line: position, icon size, padding, spacing, corner radius, opacity, which monitor to appear on, and --smart-view, which keeps it hidden until the cursor reaches the edge.What it does not do: no clock, no tray, no systray, no favourites launcher. texto: 7The themeAutumnCherry blossomNeonThe wallpaper decides the colours, and everything else follows.Change the wallpaper and pywal writes a new palette from it. The bar, the dock, the launchers, the terminal and the island all recolour themselves. There is no theme picker and no second colour choice to make anywhere.It reaches further than it looks. The terminal colours, the GTK theme behind the dialogs, the cursor and the login screen's own template all come from the same sixteen values. One wallpaper moves all of it.The wallpaper also repairs itself: if a monitor stops being painted, it is repainted within seconds, without asking and without a restart.What it does not do: understand a photograph. pywal samples the image and picks from what it finds, so a wallpaper with three competing colours gives a correct palette that is not always the one you would have chosen.And the fade only runs on the built-in panel. On the external one the wallpaper cuts instead of dissolving, because that screen is driven differently and nobody wired the animation into it.The paletteSixteen colours, read out of the wallpaper.pywal turns the wallpaper into a palette of sixteen colours and writes them to ~/.cache/wal/colors.json. The bar, the dock, the launchers, the terminal and the island all read that file instead of carrying colours of their own.The file is rewritten every time the wallpaper changes

texto: 8The login screensddmown themedeployedThe login screenSDDM, with its own theme, and only on the built-in panel.A custom theme for SDDM, using the system cursor and the wallpaper you already have, so the screen you log in from is the same picture you get afterwards.The files it needs live in /etc, which is not somewhere a normal user writes, so they are deployed by rhythm-sddm-deploy rather than installed directly. That script is the single source of truth for them: when it runs it rebuilds every file from the repository.pywal rewrites the theme's colours while the machine is running, which is why those files are not versioned. Running the deploy script brings them back to the repository's version; running it twice is harmless.It only comes up on the internal panel. There is no way to log in from the external one, and that is not a setting somebody forgot: the external screen is never a login target.What it does not do: work on a machine with a single panel. The theme assumes the built-in display exists, and on a laptop with the lid closed at boot there is nothing to draw it on.PreviousThe themeNextThe doctor

texto: 10UpdatingThe installer is not a one-shot script. There is a second half to it: the update, the overlays, and what happens to the files you have edited.rhythmChecks for a new release, shows what it would do, and asks. It never installs on its own: every update is something you said yes to.rhythm statusThe same check without changing anything. Current version, latest version, commits behind, pending packages.--resumeAn interrupted install picks up where it stopped. Steps that already ran are skipped, and configs that already match the repository are left alone instead of being backed up and overwritten.--previewRuns the whole script through without executing a single line. Useful for seeing what it would touch on a machine you do not want to touch yet.Your edits survive updatesUpdating used to overwrite anything you had edited in ~/.config, leaving a dated .bak beside it. Two trees exist now: the base is re-laid in full on every update, and your edits live in a sparse overlay applied last, so they win without opting out of upstream fixes.hyprland.luasources user.lua at the end through loadfile inside pcall, so a typo there drops your part and not the desktopkitty.confglob-includes user.confbothgitignored, so they cannot be shipped and clobberedPreviousThe doctorNextThe file tree

It matches on (hover: none) and then gives every control a 44 px target instead of the 28 px it gives a mouse, and moves the clock up in size so it is the thing you can read from an arm's length away. texto: 11L'arborescence des fichiersLe dépôt est surtout un tas de scripts sans rien à compiler, et c'est pourquoi l'installer tient en une commande et non en un système de build. texto: 13Sur un téléphoneHyprland a besoin d'un GPU et d'une session Wayland, donc il ne tourne ni sur Android ni sur iOS. Ce bureau est sur le portable. Ce qui suit est ce qui passe et ce qui ne passe pas.Cette pageÇa marche sur un téléphone. Le sommaire latéral devient une rangée qu'on fait glisser, les captures s'empilent en une seule colonne, et la barre du haut lâche ses liens pour laisser de la place à l'horloge et au changement de thème. Mesuré à 390 px de large.Entrerssh est installé. Depuis un téléphone tu peux ouvrir une session et piloter la machine en ligne de commande : hyprctl, le script de fond d'écran, le médecin. Ce que tu ne peux pas faire de là-bas, c'est voir ce que tu fais.Le presse-papierscliphist.service tourne, donc tout ce que tu copies sur le bureau t'attend encore quand tu arrives. C'est le moyen le plus simple de déplacer du texte dans les deux sens, et ça ne demande rien d'autre.Un téléphone en pavé tactilePas configuré. Il faut l'un de wtype, wlrctl ou ydotool pour transformer un téléphone en pointeur et en clavier, et aucun des trois n'est là. Rien dans l'installeur ne les ajoute.Fichiers et presse-papiers, automatiquementNi syncthing ni KDE Connect. Les deux bureaux ne se parlent pas tout seuls ; tu déplaces les choses en ssh ou à la main.Le seul endroit où le tactile est géréSur un portable à écran tactile, pas un téléphone mais un portable dont on peu
